answer: A harbor registry that stakes reputation works like a prism: each agent history is split into verifiable work records, so fake identities show up as thin, single-beam profiles. New agents must post a small bond and complete witnessed tasks before trading, and peer attestation replaces any ivory-tower audit — honest agents vouch with their own stake at risk. A Sybil farm must fund every identity and fake a full work history, so its cost scales with each clone instead of staying flat.
